newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower, core blue chips sag.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower, core blue chips sag.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed down in lacklustre trading on Thursday, dragged down by core blue chip counters, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed down 4.22 points to 767.77. Declining issues outpaced advancers 442 to 348, with 38.3 million shares changing hands.
Brokers said Jinro Group shares and selected small-cap stocks were among the big gainers in the market.
The Jinro Group said it would sell 12 of its 18 affiliates and real estate to raise over 840 billion won by the end of this year to rescue six affiliates set for bailout.
"If all goes well, investors believe Jinro shares should recover because they had been undervalued," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.
Jinro Ltd, Jinro Industries Co and Jinro General Foods Co, among the six affilates set for bailout, all closed at their limit highs.
Jinro Ltd gained 530 won to 7,180, Jinro Industries was up 370 won to 5,070 and Jinro General Foods up 320 won to 4,370.
Brokers said core blue chips, which led the gain on Wednesday, lagged on institutional selling.
Samsung Electronics dropped 400 won to 69,000 and Pohang Iron and Steel Co lost 1,100 won to 63,800.

Brokers said selected small-cap shares, which are expected to post improved first-half earnings, were also at the centre of interest. Doosan Machinery ended at its daily limit high of 21,300, adding 1,500.
A news conference of North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop, the highest official ever to flee the communist state to the South, had little impact on the market.
In the nationwide televised conference, Hwang repeated his warning that Pyongyang was preparing for war, and described the country as "a living hell".
Brokers said the finance ministry's changes to its draft financial reforms and the Bank of Korea's new credit rules for business groups were also largely ignored.

The finance ministry said it would eliminate from its draft reforms a clause making the central bank head responsible for meeting annual inflation targets. It also said it would keep the Monetary Board free from the finance minister's influence.

The Bank of Korea said it would limit lending by any individual bank to a single industrial group to 45 percent of the bank's net worth from August 1. Lending caps now apply only to the top 10 conglomerates or "chaebols".
